summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for evaluation and treatment of right renal artery stenosis, which was contributing to poorly controlled hypertension. A renal artery duplex ultrasound suggested significant narrowing, prompting an endovascular procedure. The patient underwent a successful renal arteriogram with CO2 contrast followed by placement of a non-drug-eluting stent in the right transplanted renal artery. The procedure was uncomplicated, and postoperative labs showed stable renal function. The patient was monitored for 24 hours, restarted on antihypertensives, and discharged home in stable condition with instructions for activity restrictions, wound care, and dual antiplatelet therapy. Follow-up was arranged with vascular surgery and transplant nephrology in two weeks for clinical assessment and surveillance imaging.
